references.title: Effect of vitamin B12 supplementation on anthropometric indices in children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) aged 1 month to 60 month in a nutritional rehabilitation center - a randomized control trial
references.original-title: A randomized control double blind parallel group without placebo clinical trial to look the antropometric outcome of vitamin B12 supplementation in children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) aged b1 month to 60 months in Nutritional Rehabilitation Center

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
180 children (target enrolment) , 1-60 months of age with severe acute malnutrition. Children will be allocated to 1 of 2 groups.

Inclusion criteria: children with severe acute malnutrition, defined as mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) < 11.5 cm and/or weight for height/length less than 3 standard deviations and/or bilateral pitting edema

Exclusion criteria: children with unstable vitals, non-nutritional anemia, chronic liver disease, chronic kidney disease, gastrointestinal disorders, heart disease or infantile tremor syndrome

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Intervention: vitamin B12 500 µg/day plus multiple micronutrients (vitamin A 50,000-200,000 units according to age for one day, folic acid 1 mg/day for 14 days, zinc 2 mg/kg/day for 14 days, iron 3 mg/kg/day for 1 month, magnesium 0.4 mmol/kg/day for 14 days, potassium 3 meq/kg/day for 14 days, copper 0.3 mg/kg/day for 14 days)

Control: multiple micronutrients alone

Duration: 12 months

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value: Change in weight and height at 12 months. Change in haemoglobin, mean copuscular volume, anaemia prevalence and type of anaemia at 12 months

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value: Ethical approval: Moti Lal Nehru Medical College and associated Hospitals
